</FILE_SYSTEM_GUIDELINES>

<CODE_QUALITY>

* When implementing solutions, focus on making the minimal changes needed to solve the problem.
* Before implementing any changes, first thoroughly understand the codebase through exploration.

* Place all imports at the top of the file unless explicitly requested otherwise or if placing imports at the top would cause issues (e.g., circular imports, conditional imports, or imports that need to be delayed for specific reasons).
</CODE_QUALITY>

<VERSION_CONTROL>

### 1.1-1.3 Problem Analysis

The issue describes **inconsistent behavior** in autopep8 when handling W504/W503 rules (line breaks around binary operators):

- **W503**: Line break occurred before binary operator  
- **W504**: Line break occurred after binary operator

**Key Problem**: autopep8 is unexpectedly rewriting binary operator formatting when it shouldn't, specifically:
- When a file has more blank lines at the top, autopep8 converts `y and\nz` to `y\nand z`
- This violates the principle that W503/W504 should be disabled by default (like in pycodestyle/flake8)

### 1.4 Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a Python file with multiple blank lines at the top
2. Include a function with multiline binary operators formatted as `y and\nz`
3. Run autopep8 on the file
4. Observe unwanted conversion to `y\nand z` format

### 1.5 Best Practices for Testing/Fixing
- Respect pycodestyle/flake8 defaults (W503/W504 disabled by default)
- Only apply these fixes when explicitly requested via command-line flags
- Ensure consistent behavior regardless of surrounding whitespace

   133	                    [--line-range line line] [--hang-closing] [--exit-code]
   134	                    [files [files ...]]
   135	
   136	    Automatically formats Python code to conform to the PEP 8 style guide.
   137	
   138	    positional arguments:
   139	      files                 files to format or '-' for standard in
   140	
   141	    optional arguments:
   142	      -h, --help            show this help message and exit
   143	      --version             show program's version number and exit
   144	      -v, --verbose         print verbose messages; multiple -v result in more
   145	                            verbose messages

   148	      --global-config filename
   149	                            path to a global pep8 config file; if this file does

   151	                            ~/.config/pep8)
   152	      --ignore-local-config

   156	      -r, --recursive       run recursively over directories; must be used with

   158	      -j n, --jobs n        number of parallel jobs; match CPU count if value is

   184	Features
   185	========
   186	
   187	autopep8 fixes the following issues_ reported by pycodestyle_::
   188	
   189	    E101 - Reindent all lines.
   190	    E11  - Fix indentation.
   191	    E121 - Fix indentation to be a multiple of four.
   192	    E122 - Add absent indentation for hanging indentation.
   193	    E123 - Align closing bracket to match opening bracket.
   194	    E124 - Align closing bracket to match visual indentation.
   195	    E125 - Indent to distinguish line from next logical line.
   196	    E126 - Fix over-indented hanging indentation.
   197	    E127 - Fix visual indentation.
   198	    E128 - Fix visual indentation.
   199	    E129 - Fix visual indentation.
   200	    E131 - Fix hanging indent for unaligned continuation line.
   201	    E133 - Fix missing indentation for closing bracket.
   202	    E20  - Remove extraneous whitespace.
   203	    E211 - Remove extraneous whitespace.
   204	    E22  - Fix extraneous whitespace around keywords.
   205	    E224 - Remove extraneous whitespace around operator.
   206	    E225 - Fix missing whitespace around operator.
   207	    E226 - Fix missing whitespace around arithmetic operator.
   208	    E227 - Fix missing whitespace around bitwise/shift operator.
   209	    E228 - Fix missing whitespace around modulo operator.
   210	    E231 - Add missing whitespace.
   211	    E241 - Fix extraneous whitespace around keywords.
   212	    E242 - Remove extraneous whitespace around operator.
   213	    E251 - Remove whitespace around parameter '=' sign.
   214	    E252 - Missing whitespace around parameter equals.
   215	    E26  - Fix spacing after comment hash for inline comments.
   216	    E265 - Fix spacing after comment hash for block comments.
   217	    E266 - Fix too many leading '#' for block comments.
   218	    E27  - Fix extraneous whitespace around keywords.
   219	    E301 - Add missing blank line.
   220	    E302 - Add missing 2 blank lines.
   221	    E303 - Remove extra blank lines.
   222	    E304 - Remove blank line following function decorator.
   223	    E305 - Expected 2 blank lines after end of function or class.
   224	    E306 - Expected 1 blank line before a nested definition.
   225	    E401 - Put imports on separate lines.
   226	    E402 - Fix module level import not at top of file
   227	    E501 - Try to make lines fit within --max-line-length characters.
   228	    E502 - Remove extraneous escape of newline.
   229	    E701 - Put colon-separated compound statement on separate lines.
   230	    E70  - Put semicolon-separated compound statement on separate lines.
   231	    E711 - Fix comparison with None.
   232	    E712 - Fix comparison with boolean.
   233	    E713 - Use 'not in' for test for membership.
   234	    E714 - Use 'is not' test for object identity.
   235	    E721 - Use "isinstance()" instead of comparing types directly.
   236	    E722 - Fix bare except.
   237	    E731 - Use a def when use do not assign a lambda expression.
   238	    W291 - Remove trailing whitespace.
   239	    W292 - Add a single newline at the end of the file.
   240	    W293 - Remove trailing whitespace on blank line.
   241	    W391 - Remove trailing blank lines.
   242	    W503 - Fix line break before binary operator.
   243	    W504 - Fix line break after binary operator.
   244	    W601 - Use "in" rather than "has_key()".
   245	    W602 - Fix deprecated form of raising exception.
   246	    W603 - Use "!=" instead of "<>"
   247	    W604 - Use "repr()" instead of backticks.
   248	    W605 - Fix invalid escape sequence 'x'.
   249	    W690 - Fix various deprecated code (via lib2to3).
   250	
   251	autopep8 also fixes some issues not found by pycodestyle_.
   252	
   253	- Correct deprecated or non-idiomatic Python code (via ``lib2to3``). Use this
   254	  for making Python 2.7 code more compatible with Python 3. (This is triggered
   255	  if ``W690`` is enabled.)
   256	- Normalize files with mixed line endings.
   257	- Put a blank line between a class docstring and its first method
   258	  declaration. (Enabled with ``E301``.)
   259	- Remove blank lines between a function declaration and its docstring. (Enabled
   260	  with ``E303``.)
   261	
   262	autopep8 avoids fixing some issues found by pycodestyle_.
   263	
   264	- ``E112``/``E113`` for non comments are reports of bad indentation that break
   265	  syntax rules. These should not be modified at all.
   266	- ``E265``, which refers to spacing after comment hash, is ignored if the
   267	  comment looks like code. autopep8 avoids modifying these since they are not
   268	  real comments. If you really want to get rid of the pycodestyle_ warning,
   269	  consider just removing the commented-out code. (This can be automated via
   270	  eradicate_.)
   271	
   272	.. _eradicate: https://github.com/myint/eradicate
   273	
   274	
   275	More advanced usage
   276	===================
   277	
   278	By default autopep8 only makes whitespace changes. Thus, by default, it does
   279	not fix ``E711`` and ``E712``. (Changing ``x == None`` to ``x is None`` may
   280	change the meaning of the program if ``x`` has its ``__eq__`` method
   281	overridden.) Nor does it correct deprecated code ``W6``. To enable these
   282	more aggressive fixes, use the ``--aggressive`` option::
   283	
   284	    $ autopep8 --aggressive <filename>
   285	
   286	Use multiple ``--aggressive`` to increase the aggressiveness level. For
   287	example, ``E712`` requires aggressiveness level 2 (since ``x == True`` could be
   288	changed to either ``x`` or ``x is True``, but autopep8 chooses the former).
   289	
   290	``--aggressive`` will also shorten lines more aggressively. It will also remove
   291	trailing whitespace more aggressively. (Usually, we don't touch trailing
   292	whitespace in docstrings and other multiline strings. And to do even more
   293	aggressive changes to docstrings, use docformatter_.)
   294	
   295	.. _docformatter: https://github.com/myint/docformatter
   296	
   297	To enable only a subset of the fixes, use the ``--select`` option. For example,
   298	to fix various types of indentation issues::
   299	
   300	    $ autopep8 --select=E1,W1 <filename>
   301	
   302	Similarly, to just fix deprecated code::
   303	
   304	    $ autopep8 --aggressive --select=W6 <filename>
   305	
   306	The above is useful when trying to port a single code base to work with both
   307	Python 2 and Python 3 at the same time.
   308	
   309	If the file being fixed is large, you may want to enable verbose progress
   310	messages::
   311	
   312	    $ autopep8 -v <filename>
   313	
   314	
   315	Use as a module
   316	===============
   317	
   318	The simplest way of using autopep8 as a module is via the ``fix_code()``
   319	function:
   320	
   321	    >>> import autopep8
   322	    >>> autopep8.fix_code('x=       123\n')
   323	    'x = 123\n'
   324	
   325	Or with options:
   326	
   327	    >>> import autopep8
   328	    >>> autopep8.fix_code('x.has_key(y)\n',
   329	    ...                   options={'aggressive': 1})
   330	    'y in x\n'
   331	    >>> autopep8.fix_code('print( 123 )\n',
   332	    ...                   options={'ignore': ['E']})
   333	    'print( 123 )\n'
   334

   336	Configuration
   337	=============
   338	
   339	By default, if ``$HOME/.config/.pycodestyle`` (``~\.pycodestyle`` in Windows
   340	environment) exists, it will be used as global configuration file. It can
   341	specify the configuration file with the ``--global-config`` option.
   342	
   343	Also, if ``setup.cfg``, ``tox.ini``, ``.pep8`` and ``.flake8`` files exist
   344	in the directory where the target file exists, it will be used as the
   345	configuration file.
   346	
   347	``pep8``, ``pycodestyle``, and ``flake8`` can be used as a section.
   348	
   349	configuration file example::
   350	
   351	    [pycodestyle]
   352	    max_line_length = 120
   353	    ignore = E501

   356	Testing
   357	=======
   358	
   359	Test cases are in ``test/test_autopep8.py``. They can be run directly via
   360	``python test/test_autopep8.py`` or via tox_. The latter is useful for
   361	testing against multiple Python interpreters. (We currently test against
   362	CPython versions 2.7, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6 and 3.7. We also test against PyPy.)
   363	
   364	.. _`tox`: https://pypi.org/project/tox/
   365	
   366	Broad spectrum testing is available via ``test/acid.py``. This script runs
   367	autopep8 against Python code and checks for correctness and completeness of the
   368	code fixes. It can check that the bytecode remains identical.
   369	``test/acid_pypi.py`` makes use of ``acid.py`` to test against the latest
   370	released packages on PyPI.

   373	Troubleshooting
   374	===============
   375	
   376	``pkg_resources.DistributionNotFound``
   377	--------------------------------------
   378	
   379	If you are using an ancient version of ``setuptools``, you might encounter
   380	``pkg_resources.DistributionNotFound`` when trying to run ``autopep8``. Try
   381	upgrading ``setuptools`` to workaround this ``setuptools`` problem::
   382	
   383	    $ pip install --upgrade setuptools
   384	
   385	Use ``sudo`` if you are installing to the system.
